title: Did you notice this detail in Jurassic Park???
note: The rippling glass of water. Sources: Michael Lantieri's own account (Universal's 'Glass of Water' featurette, YFBrIVCasE4), Film Stories and Guitar World on the guitar strings and the crew member on the car floor; Slashfilm, Fangoria, Far Out and Yahoo on the T-rex soaking up the rain and being blow-dried between takes. Run from the work folder holding src/ and tx/.

beats.say: If you pay attention, you'll realize the scariest moment in Jurassic Park isn't the T-rex. It's a glass of water.
The power is out, the rain is pouring, and the kids are stuck in the tour car.
Then the water starts to ripple. Every footstep gets closer, and that's how we know the T-rex is coming.
Filming this scene was a nightmare. That T-rex was real, a giant animatronic machine.
But it wasn't waterproof. In all that fake rain, its rubber skin soaked up water, got too heavy, and the T-rex started shaking on its own.
Between takes, the crew had to dry it with blow dryers and towels.
But the hardest shot in this scene wasn't the T-rex. It was that glass of water.
The idea came from Steven Spielberg himself. And the man he called was Michael Lantieri, in charge of the film's special dinosaur effects.
He called sound engineers. They tried wave machines. Nothing made those perfect rings.
So on set, they ran guitar strings through the car. And one crew member lay on the floor, plucking them on cue.
No computer graphics. Just a guitar string.
